questions.q: Tell me about a web page or React feature you built from start to finish. What did it do and what were the hard parts?
questions.looks_for: A real feature with clear scope, how they built components, state and API calls, the difficulties they faced, and how it was used or received.

questions.q: Describe a time you had to make a page work well on mobile phones as well as desktop. What did you change?
questions.looks_for: Concrete responsive work: layouts with flexbox or grid, media queries, image sizes, touch targets, testing on real devices or browser tools. Mentions results.

questions.q: Users say a page is slow to load. How would you find out why and make it faster?
questions.looks_for: Measures first with browser dev tools or Lighthouse, checks large images, big JavaScript bundles, too many requests, slow APIs and blocking scripts. Fixes the biggest cause and measures again.

questions.q: In React, when would you keep data in a component's own state, and when would you move it higher or into a shared store?
questions.looks_for: Keeps state local when only one component needs it, lifts it up when siblings share it, uses context or a store for app-wide data. Mentions avoiding unnecessary re-renders and complexity.

questions.q: What would you check to make sure a form on your website can be used by people who rely on a keyboard or screen reader?
questions.looks_for: Labels linked to inputs, logical tab order, visible focus, clear error messages, semantic HTML elements, enough colour contrast, and testing with keyboard only or a screen reader.

questions.q: A designer gives you a screen that would take a week to build exactly, but the deadline is in two days. What do you do?
questions.looks_for: Talks early with the designer and manager, proposes a simpler version that keeps the key experience, agrees what comes later, and does not silently cut corners or overwork without telling anyone.

questions.q: Why do you want to work as a front-end developer, and what do you want to grow into? Please state clearly your notice period or joining date, and your expected salary in ₹ per month or per year?
questions.looks_for: Gives a genuine reason tied to the work, a sensible growth direction, a clear notice period or joining date, and a clear salary figure or range in ₹. Honest about buyout or negotiable notice if relevant.
